surfaces.part: balusters, vertical face under the rail

Below that are horizontal tread bands that get lighter toward the bottom, so the opening shows a horizontal surface seen from above (evidence d). The railing, with a bright rail on rows 9-10 and balusters on rows 11-16, is a 6-row vertical face. Together they give a top surface and a front face of 3+ rows. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a grey stairwell with a recessed opening and about six stepped grey tones across the treads, risers and frame. It reads as a built object, not a flat sticker. The dark edge pixels are only 34% neutral, so the outline leans partly toward a tinted material tone and partly toward neutral dark grey; I call it mixed. It is not a uniform black line, because the frame is separated mostly by value. Texture is modest, with banded steps and some edge highlights but little grain. Even so, it matches or beats both shipped jp_city references on tone count and shading steps, so a careful artist would accept it next to them.
